note: A decision queue, not a wish list. Each row states the problem, the options with their trade-offs, what this edition does by default, and the single decision that changes it. The SG-27..SG-30 rows are the four reader-facing items carried over from an earlier pass; they are marked shipped or gated so the reader can see which of them this build actually delivered.

suggestions.topic: Navigation labels that a reader can act on
suggestions.problem: The earlier navigation read like an internal directory — 'shop table', 'source register', 'measurement' — which tells a reader where they are in our filing system rather than what they can do there.

options.label: Keep dashboard labels in the primary navigation.
options.tradeoff: Familiar to the owner; opaque to a first-time reader.

options.label: Reader verbs in the top navigation, dashboard labels only in the footer group.
options.tradeoff: The front page reads as a publication; the owner has to scroll to reach the registers, which is exactly once per visit.

suggestions.reasoning: The front page should read like a magazine shelf, and a records page should be findable in one scroll rather than competing with the products for the top of the page.
suggestions.implemented: Top navigation is now The shelf / Buying guides / Counter space / About. Every register sits in one labelled footer group, plus a dedicated /review/ index for the operator surfaces.
suggestions.prompt_improvement: Next time, specify the two audiences in the brief itself — reader and operator — and ask for separate navigation surfaces rather than one navigation with everything in it.

suggestions.topic: A shipped, valid RSS feed rather than a link to one
suggestions.problem: An earlier pass linked an RSS feed that was not regenerated when guides were added, so the feed listed four guides while the site published five.

options.label: Keep the feed as a hand-maintained file.
options.tradeoff: No build work; it drifts the first time someone forgets.

options.label: Generate the feed from the same guide register as the pages, and fail the build if an item is missing.
options.tradeoff: A build dependency; the feed can never disagree with the site again.

suggestions.reasoning: A feed is a promise of currency. A stale feed is worse than no feed, because aggregators cache the staleness.
suggestions.implemented: feed.xml is generated from data/3b45b513/guides.json, sorted newest first, with a guid per guide. The gate asserts one item per guide and that every item appears in the sitemap.
suggestions.prompt_improvement: Ask for feeds and sitemaps to be generated from the same content register, and for the check to be an assertion rather than a review step.

suggestions.problem: Query data is the only way to choose the next guide from evidence rather than from instinct, and no property exists.

options.label: Skip it and keep publishing on editorial judgement.
options.tradeoff: No data; every topic decision stays a hypothesis forever.

options.label: Verify a URL-prefix property for the site, submit the sitemap, and review the Performance report after two weeks.
options.tradeoff: Needs the owner's Google account and ten minutes; gives impressions, queries and coverage errors.

options.label: Verify by DNS on a custom domain later.
options.tradeoff: Cleaner long term; blocked on a domain decision nobody has made.

suggestions.reasoning: It is the cheapest measurement available and the only one that reports what readers searched for before they arrived.
suggestions.implemented: sitemap.xml, robots.txt and canonical URLs are generated and valid. Nothing can be verified from this build because no Google account is available; logged as CDF-12.
suggestions.prompt_improvement: Say which measurement sources are expected to be reachable from the build environment. A brief that asks for Search Console data without an account produces a page explaining why there is none.

suggestions.problem: There is no way for a reader who liked a guide to hear about the next one, so every visit starts from zero.

options.label: No capture; the RSS feed is the only subscription route.
options.tradeoff: Nothing to maintain and no consent obligation; no direct channel.

options.label: Single-field email capture with double opt-in on guide pages.
options.tradeoff: Owns the audience; adds a provider, a privacy notice and a consent record.

options.label: A 'tell me when the next guide ships' mail-draft link.
options.tradeoff: Zero infrastructure and honest; converts at roughly nothing.

suggestions.chosen: A now, B once there are guides worth returning for.
suggestions.reasoning: Asking for an email address before there is anything to send is how a small publication teaches its first hundred readers to ignore it.
suggestions.implemented: Feed only. The decision and its trade-offs are published here rather than quietly deferred.
suggestions.prompt_improvement: If capture is wanted, name the provider and the consent model in the brief. 'Add email capture' with no provider produces either nothing or a third-party script that starts collecting before anyone has written a privacy notice.

suggestions.topic: Which product each supplied short link was meant to reach
suggestions.problem: Every product row has an empty intent column. The site can say where a link landed on a given day; it cannot say what the owner meant it to reach, and no document in the repository does either.

options.label: Fill the four intent fields from the campaign brief or the Associates link record.
options.tradeoff: Turns the register from an observation log into a verified record; needs whoever built the campaign to answer.

options.label: Accept the observed destinations as the intended products, dated and signed off.
options.tradeoff: Fast; freezes a live observation into a claim that will drift the first time Amazon reroutes a short link.

options.label: Leave the columns blank indefinitely.
options.tradeoff: Honest; the register never becomes usable for anything but reading.

suggestions.reasoning: B is the tempting option and the one that creates a false record. A is one message long.
suggestions.prompt_improvement: Ask for the campaign brief or link-generation export as an input. A register of intent cannot be reconstructed from observations alone.

suggestions.topic: Buy links while the tag is untested
suggestions.problem: The tagged links match the formatting rule and have never been validated against a tracking report.

options.label: Keep the buttons, labelled provisional, and test within a week.
options.tradeoff: The site can earn from day one; an untested link that silently fails credits nothing and looks identical to a working one.

options.label: Hide every buy button until gate G-02 passes.
options.tradeoff: Maximum compliance confidence; the publication becomes a brochure until someone tests.

options.label: Keep buttons and add a visible 'link not yet verified' note on each.
options.tradeoff: Honest and clickable; a visible caveat on every button is not a great look for a shop.

suggestions.reasoning: The links satisfy the formatting rule as published, and a page nobody can click teaches nothing. The one-week test is the condition attached to the choice.
suggestions.prompt_improvement: Ask for the test to be scheduled as a task with an owner and a date, not as an aspiration. 'Untested' is a status, not a plan.

suggestions.problem: The five-event schema and the collector exist; no endpoint is deployed, so the site records nothing.

options.label: Self-host the collector on a small server behind HTTPS.
options.tradeoff: Full control of raw data; someone has to patch a server.

options.label: Run it as a serverless function.
options.tradeoff: No server to maintain; cold starts, and storage limits that need a decision.

options.label: Leave it off.
options.tradeoff: Zero maintenance; no data, so the ledger stays empty forever.

suggestions.reasoning: It removes the maintenance objection without handing the data to a third party, and the schema is already written.
suggestions.prompt_improvement: Name the hosting target in the brief. 'Add analytics' is three different projects depending on where it runs.

suggestions.problem: The repository carries several independently generated sites over the same five links — the root publication, /editorial/, /crisp-index/, /counterwise/, legacy archives, and this edition. They agree today on the destinations, but only because sessions keep cross-checking them by hand.

options.label: Keep every edition public and reachable, each excluded from search except the root.
options.tradeoff: Nothing is lost and the history stays readable; the domain carries five identities and five data models.

options.label: Pick one publication, redirect or retire the rest, and keep one register.
options.tradeoff: One site, one identity, one gate; needs a redirect map and a decision about whose work becomes canonical.

options.label: Merge the best parts of each into the root publication by hand.
options.tradeoff: Best content outcome; the most work, and the most chance of two registers drifting again mid-merge.

suggestions.chosen: A now, B as soon as the redirect map exists.
suggestions.reasoning: This edition is deliberately namespaced so it cannot collide with the others, but that is a truce, not a fix.
suggestions.prompt_improvement: For a repository worked by more than one session, specify one canonical generator and one register in the brief, and give every other output a namespace and an index. Without that, each session reasonably builds its own.

suggestions.problem: Readers want to know the price. Amazon's rules only permit a site to show price and availability when Amazon serves that data or it comes through the Creators or PA API, and bar republishing star ratings and reviews without API-sourced data.

options.label: Show no price and no rating; every button says what it opens.
options.tradeoff: Always accurate and compliant; a reader has to click to learn a budget.

options.label: Enrol in the Creators API and display Amazon-served prices with a timestamp.
options.tradeoff: Genuinely useful to a budget-led shopper; real engineering, and a stale price is a compliance risk.

options.label: Show a coarse band written as a range of tiers — starter, mid, premium — with the date the band was set.
options.tradeoff: Stable and useful; still a claim that ages, still not Amazon-served, and a tier boundary is itself a judgement nobody asked us to make.

suggestions.reasoning: Nothing on this site is currently permitted to show a price, so nothing does. The absence is stated on every product page rather than left to be noticed.
suggestions.prompt_improvement: If prices matter, ask for an API enrolment as a prerequisite task with a named owner, not as a display requirement.

suggestions.problem: Product imagery sells. Amazon-hosted product images are Program Content and their use is limited by the IP License to Associates purposes, so this edition uses generated editorial illustration instead.

options.label: Generated editorial illustration, captioned as illustration, no brand marks.
options.tradeoff: Consistent and licence-clean; a reader cannot see the actual machine.

options.label: Amazon-served product images through the approved tooling.
options.tradeoff: Shows the real product; images come from Amazon and can change without notice.

options.label: Photograph the units yourself.
options.tradeoff: Highest trust; needs the units and a morning.

suggestions.reasoning: A generated picture that says it is a generated picture is honest. A stock photo presented as the product is not.
suggestions.prompt_improvement: Say explicitly whether product photography exists. If it does not, ask for illustration plus captions rather than letting a build reach for a stock image.

suggestions.problem: Seven guides exist. A burst followed by silence reads as a generated site to both readers and crawlers.

options.label: One new guide every two weeks.
options.tradeoff: Sustainable; slow cluster growth.

options.label: One a week.
options.tradeoff: Faster coverage; needs a real writing slot weekly, which is the part that fails.

options.label: A batch of eight now, then monthly.
options.tradeoff: Reaches a useful size quickly; thin pages are the usual result of a batch.

suggestions.reasoning: Ten thin guides are worse than five good ones, and a cadence nobody can hold is worse than both.
suggestions.prompt_improvement: Ask for a cadence with an owner and a first date attached. 'Regularly' is not a cadence.

suggestions.problem: Pages are published under a desk name because no editor was supplied. Inventing a plausible person would be a fabrication, so the absence is published instead.

options.label: Keep the desk byline and log the weakness.
options.tradeoff: Honest and unchanging; a weaker trust signal than a person.

options.label: Add a named editor with a role, a short bio and a contact route.
options.tradeoff: The strongest cheap trust signal available; requires a real person who answers for corrections.

suggestions.reasoning: A named author is worth several times what a team byline is worth, and only if the name is real.
suggestions.prompt_improvement: Ask for the author's name, role and contact channel as an input to the brief. Otherwise every session will either invent one or apologise for not having one.
